{{Short description|American ecologist}}

'''Aaron M. Ellison''' is an American ecologist, photographer, sculptor, and writer. He retired in July 2021 after 20 years as the senior research fellow in ecology at [[Harvard University]] and as a Senior Ecologist at the [[Harvard Forest]]. He also served as deputy director of the Harvard Forest from 2018 to 2021. Until 2018, he also was an adjunct research professor at the [[University of Massachusetts]] in the Departments of Biology and Environmental Conservation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bio.umass.edu/biology/about/directories/faculty/aaron-m-ellison|title=UMass Amherst: Biology Department: Faculty: Aaron M. Ellison|website=www.bio.umass.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref> Ellison has both authored and co-authored numerous scientific papers, books, book reviews and software reviews. For more than 30 years, Ellison has studied food-web dynamics and community ecology of wetlands and forests; the evolutionary ecology of carnivorous plants; the responses of plants and ants to global climate change; application of Bayesian statistical inference to ecological research and environmental decision-making; and the critical reaction of Ecology to Modernism.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu/aaron-ellison|title=Aaron Ellison {{!}} Harvard Forest|website=harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2021-01-24}}</ref> In 2012 he was elected a fellow of the [[Ecological Society of America]]. He was the editor-in-chief of ''[[Ecological Monographs]]'' from 2008 to 2015,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://esa.org/history/esa-journals/past-journal-editors/|title=Past Journal Editors|last=ESA Historical Records Committee|website=esa.org|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref> was a senior editor of ''[[Methods in Ecology and Evolution]]'' from 2018-2021, and since 2021 has been the executive editor of ''Methods in Ecology and Evolution''. 

==Career==
Ellison was born in 1960 in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], United States. He attended [[Yale University]], where he studied East Asian studies/Asian philosophy and obtained his B.A. in 1982. He later went on to obtain his Ph.D. in ecology and evolutionary biology at [[Brown University]] in 1986. Ellison's postdoctoral positions were with the [[Organization for Tropical Studies]] in Costa Rica, Department of Biology, [[Tulane University]], 1988–1989, and [[Cornell University]], Section of Ecology and Systematics and Ecosystems Research Center, 1986–1988.<ref name=":1" />

He spent a year educating students at [[Swarthmore College]] and in 1990 he moved to a permanent position at [[Mount Holyoke College]]. At Mount Holyoke, he was an assistant, associate, and full professor of biology and environmental studies, educating students in biology, environmental studies and statistics until 2001. He also served as sponsored research officer and associate dean for science. After a year's sabbatical at [[Harvard Forest]] as a Charles Bullard Fellow,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu/mid-career-fellowships|title=Charles Bullard Fellowship|last=Harvard Forest|website=harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2021-01-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125094922/https://harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu/mid-career-fellowships|archive-date=2021-01-25|url-status=dead}}</ref> he moved to Harvard Forest as a senior ecologist in 2002.<ref name=":1" />

After retiring from Harvard in 2021, Aaron co-founded, with Manisha Patel, the company Sound Solutions for Sustainable Science, which develops and provides a range of consulting services, workshops, and programs.

*1992 – Presidential Faculty Fellow, [[National Science Foundation|U.S. National Science Foundation]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=9253743&HistoricalAwards=false|title=NSF Award Search: Award#9253743 - Presidential Faculty Fellow: Marine Environmental Ecology|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref>
*2004 – Eminent Ecologist, [[Kellogg Biological Station]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://peerj.com/AMEllison/|title=PeerJ - Profile - Aaron Ellison (AMEllison)|website=peerj.com|language=en|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref>
*2012 – Elected Fellow, Ecological Society of America<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.esa.org/programs/fellows-program/esa-fellows/|title=ESA Fellows|last=Ecological Society of America|website=esa.org|language=en|access-date=2021-01-24}}</ref>
*2014 – Human Diversity Award (for the Harvard Forest Summer Undergraduate Research Program), [[Organization of Biological Field Stations]]
*2022 - Natural Sciences Fellow, [[Swedish Collegium for Advanced Study]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Fellows SCAS |url=https://www.swedishcollegium.se/fellows/former-fellows/all-former-fellows }}</ref>
*2022 - [[Humboldt Prize]] (Humboldt Research Award)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Explore the Humboldt Network|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network?tx_solr%5Bpage%5D=90&tx_solr%5Bq%5D=Humanities&tx_solr%5Bsort%5D=electiondate_dateS%2Bdesc&cHash=a4d5584e9b2109e31f9d85262c06c30b|access-date=2022-01-31|website=www.humboldt-foundation.de|language=en}}</ref>

== Books ==
*''A primer of ecological statistics'' (1st and 2nd editions). 2004/2012. Gotelli, N. J. & A. M. Ellison. [[Oxford University Press]], New York, New York, USA.
*''A field guide to the ants of New England''. 2012. Ellison, A. M., N. J. Gotelli, G. Alpert, and E. J. Farnsworth. [[Yale University Press]], New Haven, Connecticut, USA.
*''Stepping in the same river twice: replication in biological research''. 2017. Shavit, A. & A. M. Ellison (editors). [[Yale University Press]], New Haven, Connecticut, USA.
*''Vanishing point: poetry and photography from the Pacific northwest''. 2017. Ellison, A. M. BookBaby.
*''Carnivorous plants: physiology, ecology, and evolution''[https://academic.oup.com/book/27905]. 2018. Ellison, A. M. & L. Adamec (editors). [[Oxford University Press]], Oxford, UK.
*''Causes and consequences of species diversity in forest ecosystems''. 2019. Ellison, A. M. & F. S. Gilliam (editors). [[MDPI]] Books, Basel, Switzerland.
*''Scaling in ecology in a model system''[https://press.princeton.edu/books/paperback/9780691222776/scaling-in-ecology-with-a-model-system]. 2021. Ellison, A. M. & N. J. Gotelli. ''Monographs in Population Biology'', number 64. [[Princeton University Press]], Princeton, New Jersey, USA.
